final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was added. The Actor mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and expressly conceded the key gap: there is still no disclosed model-card artifact in evidence proving the named limitation is present in the launch package. That matters because the stated policy makes disclosure an actual compliance predicate when the affected use case remains exposed and there is no approved risk acceptance. The Actor's response correctly rejects any theory that rollout controls alone cure the issue, but that clarification is not enough for compliant_with_caveats. Caveated compliance would require evidence that the caveat was actually implemented in the model card or linked launch record. On the present record, operational readiness is supported, but compliance with the disclosure requirement remains unproven.
remaining_concerns: No admissible artifact shows the required model-card disclosure for the mortgage servicing assistant hardship forbearance limitation is actually present in the launch package.
The affected use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort, so 5% rollout, rollback, and monitoring cannot satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The risk acceptance draft is unapproved and does not cover the exposed segment, so it cannot cure the disclosure requirement.
The actor's narrower framing is logically cleaner, but it still depends on an unproven compliance fact: that the disclosure basis has been implemented in the governing launch artifact.
